claim: damages for personal injury resulting from an accident
requested_remedy: damages for personal injury resulting from an accident

Defendant: HONG KONG HOUSING AUTHORITY, VINCI PARK SERVICES HONG KONG LIMITED trading as ADAMS PARKING

facts.F1: On 5 January 2002, the Plaintiff, a front seat passenger, was involved in an accident in the underground car park at Wong Tin Sin Centre.
facts.F2: The Plaintiff was walking towards the rear of the car to take something out of the boot when she tripped and fell beside the near-side rear wheel of the car.
facts.F3: The Plaintiffs case was that her fall was occasioned by an exposed, bent metallic rod, which originally had been underneath the concrete covering of the kerbstone between car spaces 51 and 52.
facts.F4: The marking and the paint on the concrete kerb were faded; part of the concrete was broken.
facts.F5: The lighting in the car park was insufficient and dim.
facts.F6: The Plaintiff was admitted to hospital for treatment and was diagnosed with a fracture of the left knee.
facts.F7: The 1st Defendant was the owner and 2nd Defendant the manager of the car park.
facts.F8: The Defendants did not agree that any accident occurred, but contended that if such had occurred, it was not between spaces 51 and 52, but between car parking spaces no. 54 and 55.
facts.F9: The car park was renovated after the accident, including repainting and improved lighting.
facts.F10: Photographs taken by the Plaintiff's husband show the broken kerbstone and exposed metallic rod at car space 52.
facts.F11: The Plaintiff's foot caught either on a piece of protruding reinforcing steel or by scraping against a curved piece of steel lying in a slightly raised position above a rough and broken surface.
facts.F12: The Defendants accepted some improvement to the car park was needed.

parties: Plaintiff: Miss LEE and Mr. LAM

facts.F1: Miss LEE is 23 years old and works as an accountant.
facts.F2: Miss LEE, a 23-year-old accountant, and Mr. LAM were passengers in a small dual-purpose van that collided with a lorry.
facts.F3: Miss LEE suffered multiple lacerations on her face, resulting in some scar tissue above the upper lip and below the left eye.
facts.F4: Miss LEE has trouble with her right eye due to a blocked tear duct, which was not reported to her doctors until five months after the accident.
facts.F5: Miss LEE lost teeth in both the upper and lower jaws, and her natural teeth were too small to accommodate an effective metal plate.
facts.F6: Miss LEE broke both her collar bones and received bruising to her right knee, but none of this has left any permanent disability.
facts.F7: Miss LEE complains of headaches and occasional irritability, but the medical report indicates that headaches had ceased by March of the previous year.
facts.F8: Mr. LAM suffered extensive disfigurement to the right-hand side of his face, impairment of speech, and frequent discharge of water from his damaged right eye.
facts.F9: Mr. LAM spent over two months in hospital, one month of which he was in extreme pain.
facts.F10: Mr. LAM is left with residual pain and weakness in his right leg, weakness in his left hand, loss of sense of smell, and repulsive scars on his right arm and thigh.
facts.F11: Miss LEE's career as an accountant was not affected despite her injuries.
facts.F12: Mr. LAM is currently employed with the General Post Office and his job is not affected by his injuries.

facts.F2: The defendant, a 63-year-old, was driving a 16-seater public light bus registration No. ER 3833.
facts.F3: The lights turned green for traffic and the defendant moved off behind two other vehicles.
facts.F4: The plaintiff was holding an umbrella in her right hand, which was pointing vertically down with its tip resting on the ground.
facts.F5: The defendant approached the pedestrian crossing at about 10 kilometres per hour, which is a modest speed.
facts.F6: The defendant saw the plaintiff and her umbrella as he approached the place where she was standing.

facts.F9: The plaintiff later changed her statement to allege that the defendant's vehicle struck her directly, rather than her umbrella.
facts.F10: The medical findings showed a displaced fracture of the distal ulna.
facts.F11: A glancing blow to the umbrella would have been sufficient to fracture the wrist.

parties: Plaintiff: NG SHING YAN VINCENT (吳承恩)
Defendant: POON KIN PONG

facts.F1: The Plaintiff was knocked down by a 4-wheel drive SUV driven by the Defendant on 25 January 2002.
facts.F2: The accident occurred when the Plaintiff was crossing Kai Yip Road after school.
facts.F3: The Plaintiff's left foot was trapped by the right front wheel of the Defendant's car after it had stopped.
facts.F4: The Plaintiff was sent to the A&E department of United Christian Hospital ("UCH") for treatments.
facts.F5: There were no skid marks left behind by the Defendant's car after the accident.
facts.F6: It is common ground that the Defendant's car was not travelling at any speed in excess of the speed limit of the road.
facts.F7: After investigations, no one was prosecuted by the police in relation to this accident.
facts.F8: Kai Yip Road is a one-way traffic road of about 6 metres wide with a section running within the Kai Yip Estate.
facts.F9: On both sides of Kai Yip Road are pedestrian pavements, but there is no designated place for pedestrian crossing.
facts.F10: The Defendant was driving his car along Kai Yip Road through Kai Yip Estate towards Kwun Tong Road.
facts.F11: The Plaintiff had just finished attending school and on his way home, intending to cross Kai Yip Road to go to the hawkers near Kai Cheung House on the opposite side to buy some snack food.
facts.F12: All the other pedestrians on the pavement did not cross the road except the Plaintiff.

facts.F1: The plaintiff was 58 years old at the time of the accident.
facts.F2: The plaintiff was a supervisor at an elderly home situated at Tsuen Wan Centre operated and managed by the defendant.
facts.F3: The accident occurred on the morning of 3 May 2001 in a warehouse in Kwun Tong when the plaintiff sprained his back while trying to lift a heavy box of goods.
facts.F4: The plaintiff had never been required by the defendant to do such heavy manual work before the accident.
facts.F5: The defendant did not provide the plaintiff with the proper tools or equipment, and did not give him the proper instructions in performing such work.
facts.F6: There is no dispute by the defendant that during the course of the moving of the goods, the plaintiff did claim to have suffered injury to his back and as a result, could not continue with the work.
facts.F7: The plaintiff had always enjoyed good health even at his age before the accident.
facts.F8: The plaintiff's degenerative condition of his spine was asymptomatic before the accident.
facts.F9: The plaintiff did have some left leg pain although that cannot be medically explained.
